Format Long Vectors and Lists as Aligned Tables with Air

Source: R/54_use_air_table_.R
use_air_table.Rd

Air (\(\geq\) 0.8.0) can align the elements of a call column by column, giving the same layout as tibble::tribble() or data.table::fcase(). The feature is switched on by the experimental # fmt: table comment directive placed right above the call, but air never re-flows the elements on its own: whatever sits on one source line stays there.

use_air_table() does the two things air does not do by itself:

  1. runs air format on path, so every long vector and list is laid out with one element per line;

  2. inserts the directive above every c() / list() call that has more than min_length elements, and re-flows the elements so that each row holds ncol of them. Multi-line definitions are collapsed by deleting the line breaks between the elements of a row; a definition that air kept on a single line is split into rows instead.

A second air format run then pads the cells and aligns the columns.

Usage

use_air_table(
  path = NULL,
  ncol = 3L,
  min_length = 12L,
  marker = "# fmt: table",
  ...
)

Arguments

path

Path to an R file to modify. If NULL and RStudio is available, the path of the active document is used.

ncol

Number of elements placed on each table row.

min_length

A vector or list is only converted when it has strictly more than this many elements.

marker

The comment directive that enables table formatting in air.

...

Additional arguments. Currently unused and must be empty.

Value

Invisibly returns the normalized path.

Details

Requirements and scope:

  • air must be installed and on the PATH (see check_air_installed()), and the directive requires air 0.8.0 or newer.

  • Only calls whose elements are all unnamed are rewritten. Air expands named elements (list(a = 1)) one per line no matter what the directive says, so named calls are skipped to avoid a marker that has no effect.

  • Calls that already carry marker on the preceding line are left untouched, so the function is idempotent.

  • Air only honours the directive on the outermost call of a statement, so a vector or list nested inside another call (for example an argument of x <- list(a = c(...))) is skipped.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
tf <- tempfile(fileext = ".R")
writeLines(
  'x <- c("alpha", "beta", "gamma", "delta", "epsilon", "zeta", "eta", "theta")',
  tf
)
use_air_table(tf, ncol = 3L, min_length = 6L)
readLines(tf) |> cli::cli_code()
} # }
